findings.text: the `tests` line and both suite `command` fields (manifest.md:21, :22) carry an unsubstituted `<worktree>` / `<scratch checkout of the orientation base>` placeholder, so the gate command promotion fills its receipt from cannot be re-run as recorded even though the logs' own headers do carry the literal command.

negative_control_log names lower-pocket.json, a measurement receipt whose own fields are the control, not a red log; the log this field is read for (a non-zero EXIT line and a failing test id) is guard-collision-check.log, so a gate reading the field finds no exit status at all.

the log names SOURCE_REVISION=c5c53edf0, whose private_flux_pocket.wall_distance still measures to wall vertices and whose angles_at_null.pair_blocks still reports the smallest-angle shift, so the c5c53edf0 code cannot have produced the 21.918 mm wall minimum in lower-pocket.json or the paired shifts in angles-at-null.json; the receipts correspond to the uncommitted tree that landed at e97c2249f, and the record's revision claim is wrong although the numbers reproduce from head.

`tip = int(np.argmax(radii))` with radii measured from the magnetic axis selects the X-point, so the receipt's state_lobe_tip_rz is the polished null and lobe_bearing_deg is the axis-to-saddle bearing; the fragment no longer prints it after the previous review, but _print_headlines (measure_promoted_nodes.py:562) still emits it and the receipt still names it a lobe, so the withdrawn reading can be re-adopted from the archive alone.

the branch table pairs the two fields' arms by ARM_NAMES, i.e. by the trace's own slot label, while the prose at promoted-nodes-xpoint-angles.html:93 attributes the pairing to each branch's reach; the two pairings coincide on this data (reaches 2.4286/2.8272/4.6619/0.9102 m) but a closed loop whose split point swaps between fields would pair lobe-out against lobe-back with no error raised.

this receipt splits the promoted set at the X-point height (`height_m > x_point_z`) while measure_promoted_nodes.py:434 splits it at zero (`heights > 0.0`), the definition the brief's 31/29 count uses; both give 31/29 here only because no promoted node lies between Z=0 and the X-point, so the two halves are one partition under two rules and would diverge silently on another state.
